name: Bolt Kit
description: A big, loud, roomy acoustic kit: 24" kick, deep floor toms, a tight steel snare, rides played as crashes, a trash stack; close mics and room as two trims, driven into saturation
source: Karoryfer Samples, CC0 1.0: Big Rusty Drums (github.com/sfzinstruments/karoryfer.big-rusty-drums) and Frankensnare (github.com/sfzinstruments/karoryfer.frankensnare), FLACs renamed and trimmed (each ends 60 dB below its own peak, 50 ms fade). The map is CC0 too
notes: Assembled 2026-11-07: a big, loud kit in a room, kick and snare up front, floor toms left, rides played as crashes, the drums run into saturation. Samples chosen by measurement.

Big Rusty Drums (Szpaderski, Poland): 24x18 kick, 22x16 / 18x16 floor toms, 15x15 and 14x14 toms, 14" hats, 22" Sabian Big & Ugly ride (bow on 51, edge as the crash-ride on 49), a three-cymbal stack (39) as a trashy crash. Frankensnare: 12x5 steel snare (38, the tightest and highest, about 276 Hz) and the 14x8 aluminium snare's rimshot (40).
Pads 48 and 50 are the 14" tom transposed +3 and +6 semitones, so General MIDI patterns find six toms.

Velocity: the steps' seven velocities (10 29 49 68 88 107 127) each play their own recording where a drum has seven layers, so rolls (x0.7 per hit) walk down through different hits; law simpler 0.15 on top. Round robin 1 of each layer only.

Mics: groups 'close' and 'room' (the overheads; cymbals play from them alone). Offsets from the libraries' own SFZ defaults: tom room -3.1 dB, snare top -4.4 dB under bottom and room, kick room -10 dB (unfiltered).

Drive: each drum mic's loudest layer goes 6 dB into the voice's tanh (drive = 6 dB minus its raw peak), the softer layers less; hats and cymbals clean. Level: each pad's top zone at -18 dB energy over its first 150 ms after drive, then the pad trims (gainDb). Toms panned by size, floor toms left; sidestick clean.
Made by scripts/sa/make-bolt-kit.py. The samples are CC0, so megalooper ships the kit with its audio, as it does the Analog Kit.
